# Affinity Mapping

Grouping research observations, one per note, into clusters by similarity, then naming each cluster. The step between raw notes and findings.

## How I do it

- One observation per sticky, in the participant's words where possible, tagged with the participant number (P1 to P12, never a name).
- Group silently first, then name the groups. Naming too early forces notes into the wrong box.
- A cluster with notes from one participant only is an anecdote, not a finding.
- On client work the board lives in the client's workspace (Copperline's FigJam), never in mine.

## Notes

- Alone it takes me about 1.5 hours per 40 observations. With [[imani-clarke|Imani]] it is faster and better; she argues about every cluster name.
- I compared my Lintel diary study map with an AI tool's clustering in September 2026 ([[ai-synthesis-trial-notes]]). The tool was faster and merged two clusters that mattered separately.
